editorial:
Imagine spending a hot summer in the French countryside right before World War II starts. You follow Marie, a 13-year-old girl who is starting to realize she isn't a little kid anymore. She travels with her parents to visit her grandparents near Avignon, and the whole movie feels like a slow, sunny dream. Marie finds herself crushing hard on a handsome Jewish doctor in town. It is a sweet but painful look at first love and that awkward stage of growing up where you feel everything way too deeply.

What really works here is how the movie captures those confusing teenage feelings. The acting is soft and natural, and the scenery is beautiful. It does move a bit slowly, so if you like non-stop action, this might not be for you. However, if you enjoy character stories, you will love it. You should definitely try to find it on a high-quality stream like Prime Video in 4K Ultra HD to see the colors of the landscape, or just grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like owning physical copies. It is a great pick for a quiet Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a sad and heavy note. Marie has to face the hard truth that the doctor does not love her back because he is actually in love with her mother, Eva. This heartbreak happens right as the world is changing. With the start of the war, the peaceful summer ends and the doctor's life becomes dangerous because he is Jewish. Marie loses her childhood innocence and realizes that love can be unfair and painful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet stories about growing up and first loves.
